source.text: Εἰ ὁ κόσμος ὑμᾶς μισεῖ, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐμὲ πρῶτον ὑμῶν μεμίσηκεν.

records.literal_gloss: If the world you hates, know that me first of you it has hated.

en.L: If the world hates you, know that it has hated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before you.
en.B: If the world hates you, know that it hated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before it hated you.
en.R: If the world hates you, understand this: it hated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before it hated you.

es.L: Si el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia, {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} que a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me ha odiado antes que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Si el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia, {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} que a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me odió antes que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Si el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia, {{plural_you:entiendan|entended}} esto: a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me odió antes que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Si le monde vous hait, sachez que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a haï avant vous.
fr.B: Si le monde vous hait, sachez qu’il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a haï avant de vous haïr.
fr.R: Si le monde vous déteste, comprenez bien ceci : il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a détesté avant de vous détester.

sw.L: Ikiwa ulimwengu unawachukia, jueni kwamba umenichukia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} kabla yenu.
sw.B: Ulimwengu ukiwachukia, jueni kwamba ulinichukia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} kwanza, kabla yenu.
sw.R: Ulimwengu ukiwachukia, elewani hili: ulinichukia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} kabla haujawachukia ninyi.

vi.L: Nếu thế gian ghét các con, hãy biết rằng nó đã ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước các con.
vi.B: Nếu thế gian ghét các con, hãy biết rằng thế gian đã ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước khi ghét các con.
vi.R: Nếu thế gian ghét các con, hãy hiểu điều này: thế gian đã ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước khi ghét các con.

ko.L: 세상이 너희를 미워하면, 세상이 너희보다 먼저 나를 미워하였다는 것을 알아라.
ko.B: 세상이 너희를 미워하거든, 세상이 너희보다 먼저 나를 미워했다는 것을 알아라.
ko.R: 세상이 너희를 미워하면 이것을 알아라. 세상은 너희를 미워하기 전에 먼저 나를 미워했다.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity organized against God
alternatives: all people, without that sense of opposition
decisions.reason: Here the world hates Jesus and his followers. This is not the world God made (1:10a) or the world God loved (3:16), but people as they set themselves against God and his messenger (7:7; 14:17; 17:14). The word recurs six times in 15:18-19, always in this sense.

decisions.choice: know: a command
alternatives: a statement: "you know that it hated me first"
decisions.reason: The form γινώσκετε is the same for "you know" and "know!". A command fits the setting: Jesus is preparing his disciples for what is coming and goes on with the command "Remember" (15:20); compare 16:1-4, where he says he tells them these things so that they will not fall away. A statement is also possible: they have already seen the world's hatred of him (7:7; 8:59; 10:31), so they know it.

decisions.choice: if the world hates you: a real case, not a mere possibility; it hated me before you: first in time, and still
decisions.reason: The "if" assumes the condition will be true: the world will hate them (17:14). The words translated "before you" mean "first, ahead of you"; Jesus has gone first along the path they will follow. The perfect tense μεμίσηκεν ("has hated") points to a hatred that began in the past and still stands.

decisions.choice: hated me before it hated you (B, R); understand this (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb ("before it hated you") so that "before you" cannot be read as "in front of you". Readable puts the command as "understand this" (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep "has hated" and "hated" as the tense allows; the Balanced past tense still describes the hatred Jesus has met.

decisions.choice: sepan (L, B); entiendan esto (R)
decisions.reason: A command (meaning decision m2), which the Spanish imperative shows.

decisions.choice: speech tenses: present, passé composé and future as in the Greek, at every level
alternatives: passé simple for the past tenses of speech
decisions.reason: This passage (15:18-27) is all Jesus's speech, so it has no narrative tense to settle; inside speech every level uses the passé composé for the past ("il m’a haï"), as people speak and as the rest of John's French does (see 1:19). The French passé composé also carries the Greek perfect's sense of a hatred that began and still stands (meaning decision m3). Where the Greek uses the present for a state that began in the past and goes on (verse 27), French does the same with "depuis".

decisions.choice: haïr (L, B); détester (R)
decisions.reason: "Haïr" is the exact word, but its forms ("il hait", "ils haïssent") are hard for young readers, so Readable says "détester" throughout 15:18-25. Literal shows the stressed "me" (meaning decision m3) with "moi, il m’a haï"; Balanced repeats the verb, as the English does, so that "avant vous" is not read as "in front of you".

decisions.choice: Ta ... các con (Jesus to the disciples); thế gian
decisions.reason: As set for the whole book: Jesus says "Ta" of himself (the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence) and "các con" to his disciples. "Thế gian" is the key term for the world as humanity set against God. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체) and gives the Father and the Spirit the honorific ("께서", -시-, "그분")
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Recorded once for 15:18-27.

source.text: εἰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἦτε, ὁ κόσμος ἂν τὸ ἴδιον ἐφίλει· ὅτι δὲ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ ἐστέ, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, διὰ τοῦτο μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος.

records.literal_gloss: If of the world you were, the world would the [its] own love; because but of the world not you are, but I chose you out of the world, on account of this hates you the world.

en.L: If you were of the world, the world would love [its] own; but because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, because of this the world hates you.
en.B: If you belonged to the world, the world would love you as its own. But you do not belong to the world; I chose you out of the world, and that is why the world hates you.
en.R: If you belonged to the world, the world would love you, because you would be its own. But you do not belong to the world. I chose you out of the world. That is why the world hates you.

es.L: Si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} del mundo, el mundo amaría lo suyo; pero como no {{plural_you:son|sois}} del mundo, sino que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} elegí del mundo, por eso el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia.
es.B: Si {{plural_you:pertenecieran|pertenecierais}} al mundo, el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} amaría como cosa suya. Pero no {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} al mundo; yo {{plural_you:los|os}} elegí y {{plural_you:los|os}} saqué del mundo, y por eso el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:pertenecieran|pertenecierais}} al mundo, el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} amaría, porque {{plural_you:serían|seríais}} suyos. Pero no {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} al mundo. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} elegí y {{plural_you:los|os}} saqué del mundo. Por eso el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odia.

fr.L: Si vous étiez du monde, le monde aimerait ce qui est sien ; mais parce que vous n’êtes pas du monde, mais que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous ai choisis hors du monde, c’est pour cela que le monde vous hait.
fr.B: Si vous apparteniez au monde, le monde vous aimerait comme ce qui est à lui. Mais vous n’appartenez pas au monde : je vous ai choisis et tirés du monde, et c’est pour cela que le monde vous hait.
fr.R: Si vous apparteniez au monde, le monde vous aimerait, parce que vous seriez à lui. Mais vous n’appartenez pas au monde. Je vous ai choisis pour vous sortir du monde. C’est pour cela que le monde vous déteste.

sw.L: Kama mngekuwa wa ulimwengu, ulimwengu ungekipenda kilicho chake; lakini kwa sababu ninyi si wa ulimwengu, bali {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliwachagua kutoka katika ulimwengu, kwa sababu hiyo ulimwengu unawachukia.
sw.B: Kama mngekuwa mali ya ulimwengu, ulimwengu ungewapenda kama walio wake. Lakini ninyi si wa ulimwengu; niliwachagua kutoka katika ulimwengu, na ndiyo sababu ulimwengu unawachukia.
sw.R: Kama mngekuwa wa ulimwengu, ulimwengu ungewapenda, kwa sababu mngekuwa wake. Lakini ninyi si wa ulimwengu. Niliwachagua kutoka katika ulimwengu. Ndiyo sababu ulimwengu unawachukia.

vi.L: Nếu các con thuộc về thế gian, thì thế gian hẳn đã yêu những gì thuộc về nó; nhưng vì các con không thuộc về thế gian, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn các con ra khỏi thế gian, vì thế thế gian ghét các con.
vi.B: Nếu các con thuộc về thế gian, thế gian hẳn đã yêu các con như người của mình. Nhưng các con không thuộc về thế gian; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn các con ra khỏi thế gian, và vì vậy thế gian ghét các con.
vi.R: Nếu các con thuộc về thế gian, thế gian sẽ yêu các con, vì các con là người của nó. Nhưng các con không thuộc về thế gian. Ta đã chọn các con ra khỏi thế gian. Vì vậy thế gian ghét các con.

ko.L: 너희가 세상에 속해 있었다면, 세상이 자기 것을 사랑하였을 것이다. 그러나 너희가 세상에 속해 있지 않고, 오히려 내가 너희를 세상에서 택하였기 때문에, 이 때문에 세상이 너희를 미워한다.
ko.B: 너희가 세상에 속해 있다면, 세상은 너희를 자기 것으로 여겨 사랑할 것이다. 그러나 너희는 세상에 속해 있지 않다. 내가 너희를 세상 가운데서 택했다. 그래서 세상이 너희를 미워하는 것이다.
ko.R: 너희가 세상에 속해 있다면, 세상은 너희를 자기 것이라고 여기고 사랑할 것이다. 그러나 너희는 세상에 속해 있지 않다. 내가 너희를 세상에서 골라냈다. 그래서 세상이 너희를 미워한다.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: they are not of the world, so the world does not love them
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes the condition is not true, as the second half says outright: "you are not of the world".

decisions.choice: of the world: belonging to it, having its source and character
decisions.reason: "Of" here means origin and belonging. Jesus says the same of himself: "I am not of this world" (8:23; 17:14, 16). The disciples still live in the world (17:11, 15), but they no longer take their life and character from it; Jesus has chosen them out of it.

decisions.choice: its own: what belongs to it; the world loves what is like itself
decisions.reason: The Greek has a neuter, "the own thing", meaning whatever belongs to the world. The world has no quarrel with what is like it; it hates Jesus because he testifies that its works are evil (7:7). The verb ἐφίλει is one of the two Greek verbs for love; John uses both for the same love (3:35; 5:20), and nothing turns on the choice here.

decisions.choice: I chose you: the disciples' separation from the world is Jesus's doing
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is emphatic. It repeats 15:16 ("you did not choose me, but I chose you"; compare 6:70; 13:18). The world's hatred comes not from anything the disciples have done but from Jesus's choice of them.

decisions.choice: belonged to the world; love you as its own (B); love you, because you would be its own (R)
decisions.reason: "Belonged to" says plainly what "of" means here (meaning decision m2). Literal brackets "its"; Balanced and Readable supply "you" as the one the world would love, which the context implies.

decisions.choice: pertenecieran al mundo; como cosa suya (B); serían suyos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decisions m2, m3).

decisions.choice: yêu (for phileo)
decisions.reason: Both Greek verbs mean "love". The world's fondness for its own is given the plain "yêu"; "yêu thương" is kept for the love Jesus commands. No difference of meaning is intended.

decisions.choice: "세상에 속해 있다" for "of the world" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "of the world" as belonging to it, with its source and character; "속하다" says belonging plainly, and "자기 것" in the same verse carries the sense of ownership.

source.text: μνημονεύετε τοῦ λόγου οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν· Οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος μείζων τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ· εἰ ἐμὲ ἐδίωξαν, καὶ ὑμᾶς διώξουσιν· εἰ τὸν λόγον μου ἐτήρησαν, καὶ τὸν ὑμέτερον τηρήσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Remember the word which I said to you: Not is a slave greater than the master of him. If me they persecuted, also you they will persecute; if the word of me they kept, also the yours they will keep.

en.L: Remember the word that I said to you: 'A slave is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they will also persecute you; if they kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, they will also keep yours.
en.B: Remember the word I spoke to you: 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If they have persecuted {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they will persecute you too. If they have kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, they will keep yours too.
en.R: Remember what I told you: 'A servant is not more important than his master.' If they treated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cruelly, they will treat you cruelly too. If they obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, they will obey yours too.

es.L: {{plural_you:Acuérdense|Acordaos}} de la palabra que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} dije: “El esclavo no es mayor que su señor”. Si a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me persiguieron, también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:los|os}} perseguirán; si guardaron mi palabra, también guardarán la {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Acuérdense|Acordaos}} de la palabra que {{plural_you:les|os}} dije: “El siervo no es más que su señor”. Si me han perseguido a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, también {{plural_you:los|os}} perseguirán a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Si han guardado mi palabra, también guardarán la {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Acuérdense|Acordaos}} de lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} dije: “Un siervo no es más importante que su señor”. Si a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me trataron con crueldad, también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:los|os}} tratarán con crueldad. Si obedecieron mi palabra, también obedecerán la {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}.

fr.L: Rappelez-vous la parole que je vous ai dite : “Un esclave n’est pas plus grand que son seigneur.” Si c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’ils ont persécuté, vous aussi, ils vous persécuteront ; si c’est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole qu’ils ont gardée, la vôtre aussi, ils la garderont.
fr.B: Rappelez-vous ce que je vous ai dit : “Un serviteur n’est pas plus grand que son maître.” S’ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont persécuté, ils vous persécuteront, vous aussi. S’ils ont gardé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole, ils garderont la vôtre de même.
fr.R: Souvenez-vous de ce que je vous ai dit : “Un serviteur n’est pas plus important que son maître.” S’ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont fait souffrir, ils vous feront souffrir, vous aussi. S’ils ont obéi à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole, ils obéiront aussi à la vôtre.

sw.L: Kumbukeni neno lile nililowaambia: 'Mtumwa si mkuu kuliko bwana wake.' Ikiwa walinitesa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, watawatesa ninyi pia; ikiwa walilishika neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, watalishika na lenu pia.
sw.B: Kumbukeni neno nililowaambia: 'Mtumishi hamzidi bwana wake.' Ikiwa wamenitesa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, watawatesa ninyi pia. Ikiwa wamelishika neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, watalishika na lenu pia.
sw.R: Kumbukeni nilichowaambia: 'Mtumishi si muhimu kuliko bwana wake.' Ikiwa walinitendea ukatili, watawatendea ukatili ninyi pia. Ikiwa walilitii neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, watalitii na lenu pia.

vi.L: Hãy nhớ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con: 'Nô lệ không lớn hơn chủ mình.' Nếu người ta đã bắt bớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, họ cũng sẽ bắt bớ các con; nếu họ đã giữ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, họ cũng sẽ giữ lời các con.
vi.B: Hãy nhớ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con: 'Đầy tớ không lớn hơn chủ mình.' Nếu người ta đã bắt bớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì họ cũng sẽ bắt bớ các con. Nếu họ đã giữ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì họ cũng sẽ giữ lời các con.
vi.R: Hãy nhớ điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con: 'Đầy tớ không quan trọng hơn chủ mình.' Nếu người ta đã đối xử tàn ác với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, họ cũng sẽ đối xử tàn ác với các con. Nếu họ đã vâng giữ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, họ cũng sẽ vâng giữ lời các con.

ko.L: 내가 너희에게 한 말을 기억하여라. '종은 자기 주인보다 크지 않다.' [그들이] 나를 박해하였으면 너희도 박해할 것이고, 내 말을 지켰으면 너희 말도 지킬 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 한 말을 기억하여라. '종은 자기 주인보다 높지 않다.' 사람들이 나를 박해했다면 너희도 박해할 것이다. 그들이 내 말을 지켰다면 너희 말도 지킬 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 한 말을 기억해라. '종은 자기 주인보다 더 중요하지 않다.' 사람들이 나를 괴롭혔다면 너희도 괴롭힐 것이다. 그들이 내 말을 따랐다면 너희 말도 따를 것이다.

decisions.choice: Jesus quotes his own saying from 13:16
decisions.reason: At the supper Jesus used the saying to teach humble service (13:16). Here he applies it to suffering: the slave shares the master's lot, so the disciples must expect the treatment Jesus has received. A slave was owned by a master and had no standing above him (8:34-35); "master" is the same word as "Lord" (13:13-14), so the disciples hear it of themselves and Jesus. Matthew 10:24-25 has a similar saying.

decisions.choice: they: the world that rejects Jesus, in John's story above all the authorities who oppose him; persecuted: pursued and harassed with hostile intent
decisions.reason: "They" has no stated subject: it is the world of 15:18-19, those who hate Jesus. In the Gospel the persecution of Jesus comes chiefly from the authorities in Jerusalem (5:16; 7:32; 11:47-53), and Jesus warns that his followers will be put out of the synagogue and even killed (16:2). The verb ἐδίωξαν is to pursue someone in order to harm them.

decisions.choice: if they kept my word: a real condition with a sober edge; the disciples' word will be received as Jesus's was, refused by most and kept by some
alternatives: ironic: they did not keep his word, so they will not keep yours
simply hopeful: they will keep your word as they kept mine
hostile: "if they watched my word", spying on it
decisions.reason: The two clauses are parallel. The first is certainly true (they persecuted Jesus), and the setting is hostility, so the second may be said with irony: the world did not keep Jesus's word (8:37, 51-52; 12:48). But some did keep it (17:6), and others will believe through the disciples' word (17:20). Reading the sentence as a real condition keeps both sides: as it went with Jesus, so it will go with them. The verb ἐτήρησαν means to keep, hold to, obey, as in 8:51; 14:23-24; it is not "to watch closely" here.

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R); master; 'A slave/servant is not greater (L, B) / more important (R) than his master' as in 13:16
decisions.reason: The quotation repeats the saying of 13:16, so each level uses the same English it used there, letting readers see that Jesus is quoting himself. "Servant" in Balanced and Readable and "slave" in Literal, as the style guide has it; meaning decision m1 keeps that a slave was owned. "His" refers to the figure in the saying and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: treated me cruelly; obeyed my word
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "persecute" (meaning decision m2) and of "keep" a word (meaning decision m3) in common words, and keeps "if" so that the second sentence stays as open as the Greek.

decisions.choice: the saying in the words of 13:16, at each level
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes his own saying (meaning decision m1), so each level repeats its own Spanish of 13:16 exactly. The quotation takes inner marks, since the speech that opens at 14:23 is still open.

decisions.choice: los trataron con crueldad; obedecieron
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Un esclave (L) / Un serviteur (B, R) n’est pas plus grand (L, B) / plus important (R) que son maître
alternatives: Le serviteur n’est pas au-dessus de son maître
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes his own saying of 13:16 (meaning decision m1), so each level should use the same French it used there; a reviewer should check the two passages against each other, since they were drafted separately. "Esclave" at Literal and "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable follow the French brief, and "maître" is the owner, as in 15:15. Literal shows the stressed "me" with "c’est moi qu’ils ont persécuté", and puts both halves in the Greek order.

decisions.choice: the saying of 13:16 in the same words at each level
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes his own saying from 13:16 (meaning note m1), so each level repeats its Swahili from there.

decisions.choice: bắt bớ (L, B); đối xử tàn ác (R)
decisions.reason: "Bắt bớ" is the familiar word for pursuing and harassing believers; Readable says what it means in everyday words.

decisions.choice: the saying worded as the Korean of 13:16: "크지 않다" (L), "높지 않다" (B), "더 중요하지 않다" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes his own saying from 13:16 (meaning decision), so Korean repeats the wording used there at each level.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα πάντα ποιήσουσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασιν τὸν πέμψαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: But these things all they will do to you on account of the name of me, because not they know the [one] having sent me.

en.L: But all these things they will do to you on account of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, because they do not know the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: But all this they will do to you on account of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, because they do not know the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: They will do all this to you because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They do it because they do not know the Father, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Pero todo esto {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} harán por causa de mi nombre, porque no conocen al que me envió.
es.B: Pero todo esto {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} harán por causa de mi nombre, porque no conocen al que me envió.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} harán todo esto porque {{plural_you:ustedes me pertenecen|vosotros me pertenecéis}}. Lo harán porque no conocen al Padre, que me envió.

fr.L: Mais toutes ces choses, ils vous les feront à cause de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, parce qu’ils ne connaissent pas celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.B: Mais tout cela, ils vous le feront à cause de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, parce qu’ils ne connaissent pas celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.R: Ils vous feront tout cela parce que vous êtes à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Ils le font parce qu’ils ne connaissent pas le Père, qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.

sw.L: Lakini mambo haya yote watawatendea kwa sababu ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, kwa kuwa hawamjui yule aliyenituma.
sw.B: Lakini haya yote watawatendea kwa sababu ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, kwa sababu hawamjui yule aliyenituma.
sw.R: Watawatendea haya yote kwa sababu ninyi ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Wanafanya hivyo kwa sababu hawamjui Baba, aliyenituma.

vi.L: Nhưng họ sẽ làm mọi điều này với các con vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì họ không biết Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Nhưng họ sẽ làm tất cả những điều đó với các con vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì họ không biết Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Họ sẽ đối xử với các con như vậy vì các con thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Họ làm thế vì họ không biết Cha, là Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러나 이 모든 것을 그들이 내 이름 때문에 너희에게 할 것이다. 그들이 나를 보내신 분을 알지 못하기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 내 이름 때문에 너희에게 이 모든 일을 할 것이다. 나를 보내신 분을 알지 못하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그들은 너희가 내게 속해 있다는 이유로 너희에게 이 모든 일을 할 것이다. 그들이 그렇게 하는 것은 나를 보내신 아버지를 알지 못하기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: on account of my name: because the disciples bear Jesus's name, that is, because they belong to him
alternatives: because they speak in his name
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. The disciples will suffer not for their own sake but because they are known as Jesus's, just as they will ask in his name (14:13-14; 15:16). Compare Matthew 10:22 and Acts 5:41.

decisions.choice: they do not know the one who sent me: the root of the world's hatred is that it does not know the Father
decisions.reason: "The one who sent me" is the Father (5:37; 8:16-18). Jesus has told his opponents that they know neither him nor his Father (7:28; 8:19, 54-55), and he repeats it in 16:3. Not knowing God, they do not recognize the one he has sent. "They" are the same people as in 15:20, the world that rejects Jesus.

decisions.choice: but: turning from the parallel sayings of 15:20 to their reason
alternatives: a strong contrast with the last clause of 15:20
decisions.reason: The word marks a turn from what will happen to why it will happen; it does not cancel the hope that some will keep the disciples' word.

decisions.choice: because you belong to me; the Father, who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of the name (meaning decision m1) and names the Father, who in John is always "the one who sent me" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: porque ustedes me pertenecen; al Padre
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

source.text: εἰ μὴ ἦλθον καὶ ἐλάλησα αὐτοῖς, ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ εἴχοσαν· νῦν δὲ πρόφασιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: If not I had come and spoken to them, sin not they would have; now but excuse not they have concerning the sin of them.

en.L: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
en.B: Had I not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin. But as it is, they have no excuse for their sin.
en.R: If I had not come and talked to them, they would not be guilty of this sin. But I have come, so they have no excuse for their sin.

es.L: Si yo no hubiera venido ni les hubiera hablado, no tendrían pecado; pero ahora no tienen excusa por su pecado.
es.B: Si yo no hubiera venido a hablarles, no tendrían pecado. Pero ahora no tienen excusa por su pecado.
es.R: Si yo no hubiera venido a hablarles, no serían culpables de este pecado. Pero yo vine, así que no tienen excusa por su pecado.

fr.L: Si je n’étais pas venu et ne leur avais pas parlé, ils n’auraient pas de péché ; mais maintenant, d’excuse pour leur péché, ils n’en ont pas.
fr.B: Si je n’étais pas venu leur parler, ils n’auraient pas de péché. Mais en fait, leur péché est sans excuse.
fr.R: Si je n’étais pas venu leur parler, ils ne seraient pas coupables de ce péché. Mais je suis venu, alors ils n’ont pas d’excuse pour leur péché.

sw.L: Kama sikuwa nimekuja na kuzungumza nao, dhambi wasingekuwa nayo; lakini sasa hawana kisingizio kuhusu dhambi yao.
sw.B: Kama nisingekuja na kuzungumza nao, wasingekuwa na dhambi. Lakini ilivyo sasa, hawana kisingizio kwa dhambi yao.
sw.R: Kama nisingekuja na kuzungumza nao, wasingekuwa na hatia ya dhambi hii. Lakini nimekuja, kwa hiyo hawana kisingizio kwa dhambi yao.

vi.L: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã không đến và nói với họ, thì họ hẳn không có tội; nhưng bây giờ họ không có cớ gì để chữa tội mình.
vi.B: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không đến và nói với họ, họ đã không có tội. Nhưng thật ra, họ không thể bào chữa cho tội mình.
vi.R: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không đến và nói với họ, họ đã không mắc tội này. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đến, nên họ không có cớ gì để bào chữa cho tội mình.

ko.L: 내가 와서 그들에게 말하지 않았다면, 그들에게 죄가 없었을 것이다. 그러나 이제는 그들이 자기 죄에 대하여 핑계가 없다.
ko.B: 내가 와서 그들에게 말하지 않았더라면 그들에게 죄가 없었을 것이다. 그러나 이제는 그들이 자기 죄를 두고 핑계를 댈 수 없다.
ko.R: 내가 와서 그들에게 말하지 않았다면, 그들은 이 죄에 대한 책임이 없었을 것이다. 그러나 나는 왔다. 그러니 그들은 자기 죄에 대해 핑계를 댈 수 없다.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: Jesus has come and spoken to them
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes the condition is not true. "Now" in the second half is logical, not a point in time: "but as things are", since he did come.

decisions.choice: to have sin: to be guilty of sin
decisions.reason: As in 9:41, John uses the phrase for guilt a person must answer for (also 15:24; 19:11). Jesus does not mean that without his coming they would be sinless, but that they would not bear this guilt.

decisions.choice: their sin: refusing to believe the Son when he came and spoke to them
decisions.reason: The sin in view is the one Jesus names in 16:9: "they do not believe in me". They heard his word ("spoken to them") and turned from it, so they cannot plead ignorance; this is the light come into the world that people refused (3:19). "Them" are those who reject him, as in 15:20-21. The word πρόφασιν means a plea or pretext offered as an excuse.

decisions.choice: would have no sin; as it is (B); would not be guilty of this sin; But I have come, so (R)
alternatives: would not have sin; but now (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "as it is" for the logical "now" (meaning decision m1) and the inverted "Had I not" for "if I had not". Readable says plainly what having sin means and which sin is meant (meaning decisions m2, m3), and spells out what "now" implies, that Jesus did come.

decisions.choice: no serían culpables de este pecado; Pero yo vine
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decisions m2, m3). "Les" here is "to them", not "to you", so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: Mais en fait
decisions.reason: The "now" is logical, not a point in time (meaning decision m1): "en fait" says "but as things are". Literal keeps "maintenant", which French also uses in this sense. The same applies in verse 24.

decisions.choice: kuwa na dhambi (L, B), kuwa na hatia ya dhambi hii (R); kisingizio
decisions.reason: "To have sin" means to be guilty of sin (meaning note m2); Literal and Balanced keep the idiom, and Readable says "guilty", as the English does. "Kisingizio" is a pretext or excuse put forward, the word's sense. The same in verse 24.

source.text: ὁ ἐμὲ μισῶν καὶ τὸν πατέρα μου μισεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] me hating also the Father of me hates.

en.L: The one who hates {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} hates {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father also.
en.B: Whoever hates {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} hates {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father as well.
en.R: Anyone who hates {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} also hates {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father.

es.L: El que me odia a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, odia también a mi Padre.
es.B: El que me odia a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, odia también a mi Padre.
es.R: Cualquiera que me odia a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} también odia a mi Padre.

fr.L: Celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} hait hait aussi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père.
fr.R: Celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} déteste déteste aussi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père.

sw.R: Mtu yeyote anayenichukia anamchukia pia Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

vi.L: Người nào ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì cũng ghét Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ai ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì cũng ghét Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ai ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cũng ghét Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 나를 미워하는 사람은 내 아버지도 미워한다.
ko.B: 나를 미워하는 사람은 누구든지 내 아버지도 미워하는 것이다.
ko.R: 누구든지 나를 미워하는 사람은 내 아버지도 미워하는 것이다.

decisions.choice: to hate the Son is to hate the Father, because the Father is present and known in him
decisions.reason: The Son and the Father are one (10:30); whoever has seen Jesus has seen the Father (12:45; 14:9), and whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him (5:23). So there is no hating Jesus while claiming to love God (8:42).

decisions.choice: the one who hates: anyone at all who hates, not one particular person
decisions.reason: The article with a participle makes a general statement, true of every case.

decisions.choice: Whoever (B); Anyone who (R)
decisions.reason: The general sense (meaning decision m2) is clearer in English with "whoever" or "anyone who", which apply to men and women alike, so no gender setting is needed.

decisions.choice: Cualquiera que
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

source.text: εἰ τὰ ἔργα μὴ ἐποίησα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἃ οὐδεὶς ἄλλος ἐποίησεν, ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ εἴχοσαν· νῦν δὲ καὶ ἑωράκασιν καὶ μεμισήκασιν καὶ ἐμὲ καὶ τὸν πατέρα μου.

records.literal_gloss: If the works not I had done among them which no one other did, sin not they would have; now but both they have seen and have hated both me and the Father of me.

en.L: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father.
en.B: Had I not done among them works that no one else has done, they would have no sin. But as it is, they have seen, and they have hated, both {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father.
en.R: If I had not done things among them that no one else has ever done, they would not be guilty of this sin. But they have seen {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father at work, and they have hated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father.

es.L: Si yo no hubiera hecho entre ellos las obras que ningún otro hizo, no tendrían pecado; pero ahora han visto, y han odiado, tanto a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como a mi Padre.
es.B: Si yo no hubiera hecho entre ellos obras que nadie más ha hecho, no tendrían pecado. Pero ahora han visto, y han odiado, tanto a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como a mi Padre.
es.R: Si yo no hubiera hecho entre ellos cosas que nadie más ha hecho jamás, no serían culpables de este pecado. Pero ellos me han visto actuar a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y a mi Padre, y nos han odiado a los dos.

fr.L: Si je n’avais pas fait parmi eux les œuvres que personne d’autre n’a faites, ils n’auraient pas de péché ; mais maintenant, ils ont vu, et ils ont haï, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} comme {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père.
fr.B: Si je n’avais pas accompli parmi eux des œuvres que nul autre n’a accomplies, ils n’auraient pas de péché. Mais en fait, ils ont vu, et ils ont haï, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi bien que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père.
fr.R: Si je n’avais pas fait parmi eux des choses que personne d’autre n’a jamais faites, ils ne seraient pas coupables de ce péché. Mais ils ont vu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} à l’œuvre, et ils ont détesté {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père comme {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Kama sikuwa nimefanya miongoni mwao kazi ambazo hakuna mwingine aliyezifanya, dhambi wasingekuwa nayo; lakini sasa wameona, tena wamechukia, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} pia.
sw.B: Kama nisingefanya miongoni mwao kazi ambazo hakuna mwingine amefanya, wasingekuwa na dhambi. Lakini ilivyo sasa, wameona, na wamechukia, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} pia.
sw.R: Kama nisingefanya miongoni mwao mambo ambayo hakuna mtu mwingine amewahi kufanya, wasingekuwa na hatia ya dhambi hii. Lakini wametuona {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} tukifanya kazi, nao wametuchukia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

vi.L: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã không làm giữa họ những công việc mà chưa ai khác làm, thì họ hẳn không có tội; nhưng bây giờ họ đã thấy và đã ghét cả {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lẫn Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không làm giữa họ những việc chưa ai khác từng làm, họ đã không có tội. Nhưng thật ra họ đã thấy, và họ đã ghét, cả {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lẫn Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không làm giữa họ những việc mà chưa ai từng làm, họ đã không mắc tội này. Nhưng họ đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hành động, và họ đã ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 다른 아무도 하지 않은 일들을 내가 그들 가운데서 하지 않았다면, 그들에게 죄가 없었을 것이다. 그러나 이제 그들은 나와 내 아버지를 보기도 하였고 미워하기도 하였다.
ko.B: 아무도 한 적이 없는 일들을 내가 그들 가운데서 하지 않았더라면, 그들에게 죄가 없었을 것이다. 그러나 이제 그들은 나와 내 아버지를 보았고, 또 미워하였다.
ko.R: 아무도 한 적 없는 일들을 내가 그들 가운데서 하지 않았다면, 그들은 이 죄에 대한 책임이 없었을 것이다. 그러나 그들은 나와 내 아버지께서 일하시는 것을 보았다. 그런데도 나와 내 아버지를 미워했다.

decisions.choice: the works: Jesus's deeds, including his signs, which are the Father's works done through him
decisions.reason: Jesus calls his deeds the works the Father gave him to do (5:36; 10:25, 32, 37-38; 14:10-11). They are unlike anyone else's: no one has ever opened the eyes of a man born blind (9:32). As 15:22 spoke of his words, this verse speaks of his deeds; both leave his hearers without excuse.

decisions.choice: to have sin: to be guilty of sin, as in 15:22
decisions.reason: The same contrary-to-fact form and the same phrase as 15:22. The guilt is that of refusing what they have seen; "now" is again logical ("but as it is").

decisions.choice: both verbs take "me and my Father": they have seen the Father in Jesus, and hated both
alternatives: they have seen the works, and have hated me and my Father
decisions.reason: The Greek pairs the verbs with "both ... and" and then pairs the objects the same way, so the most natural reading is that the people have seen Jesus and the Father as well as hated them. In Jesus's works the Father is seen (14:9-11; 12:45). Their guilt is that they have seen and still hated. The perfect tenses describe a settled state, not a passing reaction.

decisions.choice: as it is (B); things ... that no one else has ever done; this sin; at work (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "things" for "works" in plain words, and "this sin" as in 15:22. It adds "at work" to show where they saw the Father, in Jesus's deeds (meaning decisions m1, m3); this goes slightly beyond the words, though not beyond the sense.

decisions.choice: han visto, y han odiado, tanto a mí como a mi Padre
decisions.reason: Both verbs take "me and my Father" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: jamás; este pecado; actuar; nos ... a los dos
decisions.reason: As in English.

decisions.choice: ils ont vu, et ils ont haï, moi comme mon Père (L); moi aussi bien que mon Père (B)
alternatives: et ils ont vu et ils ont haï et moi et mon Père
decisions.reason: The Greek pairs both verbs and both objects with "both ... and", so that the two verbs share the two objects (meaning decision m3). French "et ... et" twice would be heavy; setting the verbs off with commas and joining the objects with "comme" or "aussi bien que" keeps both pairs. The stressed "moi" is Jesus and takes the deity_pronoun setting.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ἵνα πληρωθῇ ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ αὐτῶν γεγραμμένος ὅτι Ἐμίσησάν με δωρεάν.

records.literal_gloss: But that may be fulfilled the word the [one] in the law of them having been written, "They hated me freely."

en.L: But [this is] so that the word that has been written in their Law may be fulfilled: 'They hated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} without a cause.'
en.B: But this has happened so that the word written in their Law would be fulfilled: 'They hated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for no reason.'
en.R: But this happened so that what is written in their own Law would come true: 'They hated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for no reason.'

es.L: Pero [esto es] para que se cumpla la palabra que está escrita en su ley: “Me odiaron sin causa”.
es.B: Pero esto ha sucedido para que se cumpla la palabra escrita en su ley: “Me odiaron sin razón”.
es.R: Pero esto sucedió para que se cumpliera lo que está escrito en su propia ley: “Me odiaron sin razón”.

fr.L: Mais [c’est] pour que soit accomplie la parole qui a été écrite dans leur Loi : “Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont haï gratuitement.”
fr.B: Mais cela s’est produit pour que se réalise ce qui est écrit dans leur Loi : “Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont haï sans raison.”
fr.R: Mais c’est arrivé pour que se réalise ce qui est écrit dans leur propre Loi : “Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont détesté sans aucune raison.”

sw.L: Lakini [ni] ili litimie neno lililoandikwa katika sheria yao: 'Walinichukia bila sababu.'
sw.B: Lakini hili limetokea ili litimie neno lililoandikwa katika sheria yao: 'Walinichukia bila sababu.'

vi.L: Nhưng [điều này xảy ra] để lời đã chép trong luật pháp của họ được ứng nghiệm: 'Họ đã ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vô cớ.'
vi.B: Nhưng điều này đã xảy ra để lời chép trong luật pháp của họ được ứng nghiệm: 'Họ ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vô cớ.'
vi.R: Nhưng điều này đã xảy ra để lời chép trong chính luật pháp của họ trở thành sự thật: 'Họ ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chẳng vì lý do gì.'

ko.L: 그러나 [이것은] 그들의 율법에 기록된 말씀, 곧 '그들이 이유 없이 나를 미워하였다'는 [말씀이] 이루어지게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 이것은 그들의 율법에 '그들이 까닭 없이 나를 미워하였다'라고 기록된 말씀이 이루어지게 하려고 일어난 일이다.
ko.R: 그러나 이 일은 그들의 율법에 '그들이 아무 이유 없이 나를 미워했다'라고 쓰여 있는 말씀이 이루어지게 하려고 일어났다.

decisions.choice: an incomplete sentence: "but [this happened] so that"
alternatives: a command: "but let the word be fulfilled"
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with "but so that" and leaves the main verb unstated, as John does in 1:8, 9:3 and 13:18. The sense is supplied from what has just been said: their hatred has come about so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 35:19 or Psalm 69:5 (68:5 in the Greek Old Testament)
decisions.reason: Both psalms speak of those who hate the psalmist without cause, in words very close to the Greek here; Psalm 109:3 is similar. Psalm 69 is the psalm of the righteous sufferer that John also quotes in 2:17 ("Zeal for your house will consume me") and echoes in 19:28-29. What the psalmist suffered, Jesus suffers in full.

decisions.choice: their Law: the Scriptures as a whole, which the people themselves hold sacred
alternatives: the five books of Moses only
a Law that Jesus does not regard as his own
decisions.reason: The Psalms are not in the books of Moses, yet Jesus calls them "Law", as in 10:34, where he quotes Psalm 82 as "your Law". "Their" stresses that the very Scriptures they claim to keep describe what they are doing; it does not distance Jesus from Scripture, which he says "cannot be broken" (10:35).

decisions.choice: without cause: for no reason at all
decisions.reason: The word δωρεάν means "as a gift, for nothing"; here, hatred given for nothing, with no wrong to deserve it.

decisions.choice: [this is] (L); this has happened (B); this happened (R)
decisions.reason: English needs a main verb that the Greek leaves out (meaning decision m1). Literal brackets it; Balanced and Readable supply it plainly, as in 13:18. "Law" is capitalized because it names the Scriptures (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: [esto es] (L); esto ha sucedido (B); esto sucedió (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1). "Ley" lowercase for the Scriptures as a whole, as at 10:34 and 12:34.

decisions.choice: gratuitement (L); sans raison (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "as a gift, for nothing", and here hatred given for no reason (meaning decision m4). French "gratuitement" has the same two senses ("free of charge" and "for no reason", as in "une haine gratuite"), so Literal can keep the word's picture; Balanced and Readable give the sense plainly.

decisions.choice: sheria yao, lowercase
decisions.reason: "Sheria" is lowercase, as the style sheet asks and as at 10:34 ("sheria yenu"), though the English capitalises "Law". Here it means the Scriptures as a whole (meaning note m3), since the words come from the Psalms; "Torati" would point to the five books of Moses only.

decisions.choice: "Ta" in the quoted psalm
decisions.reason: In the psalm the speaker says "tôi"; Jesus applies the words to himself, so they take his own "Ta", with the deity_pronoun span as in the English. "Luật pháp" stays lowercase as the style guide sets.

source.text: Ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ παράκλητος ὃν ἐγὼ πέμψω ὑμῖν παρὰ τοῦ πατρός, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας ὃ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται, ἐκεῖνος μαρτυρήσει περὶ ἐμοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: When comes the advocate whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of the truth which from the Father goes out, that one will testify concerning me;

en.L: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who comes out from the Father, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: The Advocate, whom I will send to you from the Father, is the Spirit of truth, who comes out from the Father. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I will send the Advocate to you from the Father. He is the Spirit of truth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes from the Father. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Cuando venga el Defensor, a quien yo {{plural_you:les|os}} enviaré de parte del Padre, el Espíritu de la verdad, que sale del Padre, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dará testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}};
es.B: El Defensor, a quien yo {{plural_you:les|os}} enviaré de parte del Padre, es el Espíritu de la verdad, que sale del Padre. Cuando venga, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dará testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Yo {{plural_you:les|os}} enviaré de parte del Padre al Defensor. Es el Espíritu de la verdad, y viene del Padre. Cuando venga, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dará testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Quand viendra le Défenseur, que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous enverrai d’auprès du Père, l’Esprit de la vérité, qui sort d’auprès du Père, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rendra témoignage à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet ;
fr.B: Le Défenseur, que je vous enverrai d’auprès du Père, c’est l’Esprit de vérité, qui sort d’auprès du Père. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rendra témoignage à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet.
fr.R: Je vous enverrai le Défenseur de la part du Père. Il est l’Esprit de vérité, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient du Père. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} témoignera pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Atakapokuja yule Mtetezi, ambaye {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitamtuma kwenu kutoka kwa Baba, yaani Roho wa kweli, anayetoka kwa Baba, huyo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atashuhudia kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}};
sw.B: Mtetezi, ambaye nitamtuma kwenu kutoka kwa Baba, ndiye Roho wa kweli, anayetoka kwa Baba. Atakapokuja, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atashuhudia kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.R: Nitamtuma Mtetezi kwenu kutoka kwa Baba. Yeye ni Roho wa kweli, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anatoka kwa Baba. Atakapokuja, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atashuhudia kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.

vi.L: Khi Đấng Biện Hộ đến, là Đấng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai đến với các con từ nơi Cha, tức là Thánh Linh của chân lý, Đấng ra từ Cha, chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}};
vi.B: Đấng Biện Hộ mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai đến với các con từ nơi Cha, chính là Thánh Linh của chân lý, Đấng ra từ Cha. Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ta sẽ sai Đấng Biện Hộ từ nơi Cha đến với các con. Ngài là Thánh Linh của chân lý, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến từ Cha. Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 내가 아버지께로부터 너희에게 보낼 변호자, 곧 아버지께로부터 나오시는 진리의 영이 오시면, 그분께서 나에 대하여 증언하실 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 아버지께로부터 너희에게 보낼 변호자는 아버지께로부터 나오시는 진리의 영이시다. 그분께서 오시면 나에 대하여 증언하실 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 아버지께로부터 변호자를 너희에게 보낼 것이다. 그분은 진리의 영이시고, 아버지께로부터 오신다. 그분께서 오시면 나에 대하여 증언하실 것이다.

decisions.choice: the Advocate: one called to stand beside another and speak for them
decisions.reason: The word παράκλητος was used of someone called in to stand by a person, above all in a court. Here the setting is a trial: the world has hated Jesus without cause (15:25), and the Advocate comes to testify about him (compare 16:8-11). It is the same title as in 14:16 and 14:26.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of truth: the Holy Spirit, who comes from the God of truth and makes the truth known
alternatives: a spirit or attitude of truthfulness
decisions.reason: This is the Advocate already promised and named "the Spirit of truth" (14:17) and "the Holy Spirit" (14:26). He testifies to Jesus, who is the truth (14:6), and guides the disciples into all the truth (16:13).

decisions.choice: the pronouns change with the nouns they agree with; the Spirit is spoken of as a person
alternatives: the neuter means the Spirit is an impersonal force
decisions.reason: The pronoun ὃν ("whom") is masculine, agreeing with "Advocate". The pronoun ὃ ("who") is neuter, agreeing with "Spirit", a neuter noun in Greek; this is grammatical agreement and says nothing about whether the Spirit is a thing (as in 14:17, 26). The masculine ἐκεῖνος ("that one") takes up the Advocate again and is emphatic: he, and no other, will testify. What shows the Spirit as a person is what he does: he is sent, comes and testifies.

decisions.choice: comes out from the Father: in this context, the Spirit's coming on his mission from the Father, as the one Jesus sends
alternatives: a statement about the Spirit's eternal origin within God
decisions.reason: In the same sentence Jesus says that he will send the Advocate from the Father, and that the Spirit comes out from the Father; elsewhere the Father sends him at Jesus's request and in Jesus's name (14:16, 26), and Jesus sends him (16:7). In context the verb ἐκπορεύεται ("comes out, goes out") describes the Spirit's coming to the disciples from the Father. Later Christian theology drew on this verse in speaking of the Spirit's eternal relation to the Father; the Nicene Creed of 381 uses its words, and whether the Spirit proceeds from the Father alone or from the Father and the Son became a long dispute between the Eastern and Western churches. The verse itself speaks of the Spirit coming from the Father and being sent by Jesus.

decisions.choice: testify about me: bear witness to who Jesus is, as in a trial
decisions.reason: Testimony is a thread through John: John the Baptist, Jesus's works, the Father and the Scriptures testify about Jesus (5:31-39). The Spirit will continue that testimony before the world that hates him, together with the disciples (15:27) and through them (16:8-11).

decisions.choice: the Advocate
decisions.reason: The book uses "the Advocate" at every level, because John's setting is testimony and judgment (meaning decision m1). Other well-known renderings are Helper, Counselor and Comforter; each catches part of the sense.

decisions.choice: whom; who; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The Spirit is never "it" in this translation. The neuter Greek pronoun is grammatical agreement only (meaning decision m3), so English uses the personal "who", "whom" and "he". "He" takes the deity pronoun setting like every pronoun for God; the relatives "who" and "whom" do not, as nowhere else in the translation does a relative pronoun take it.

decisions.choice: comes out from (L, B); comes from (R)
decisions.reason: "Comes out" is the plain sense of the verb and keeps the link with "comes" at the start of the verse. "Proceeds", the wording of older translations and of the creed, is given in a footnote (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: The Advocate ... is the Spirit of truth. When he comes, he will testify (B); I will send the Advocate ... He is the Spirit of truth ... When he comes (R)
alternatives: one sentence in the Greek order (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence opens with "when he comes", then names the Advocate twice before reaching its main verb. Balanced and Readable first say who the Advocate is (the words in apposition, "the Spirit of truth", become "is the Spirit of truth") and then say what he will do, so the main statement is not lost; the meaning is unchanged.

decisions.choice: Defensor
sale del Padre (L, B); viene del Padre (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, the plain verb keeps away from the creedal "procede" (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: a quien, que (no setting); {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
decisions.reason: Relative pronouns take no setting; the stressed "él" for the Spirit does.

decisions.choice: le Défenseur
decisions.reason: The book-wide French word for this title, as in 14:16, where the choice and the other renderings are explained. Here the setting is a trial (meaning decision m1), which "Défenseur" fits well.

decisions.choice: qui sort d’auprès du Père (L, B); qui vient du Père (R); que ... qui ... lui, il (L)
decisions.reason: "Sortir" is the plain sense of the verb, and "d’auprès du" matches the preposition in "je vous enverrai d’auprès du Père", so the two clauses stay parallel (meaning decision m4); "procède", the wording of the Creed, is given in the footnote of m4. French "que" and "qui" have no gender, so the change of Greek pronouns (m3) needs nothing in French; Literal gives the stressed "that one" with "lui, il", pronouns for the Spirit with the deity_pronoun setting. Readable says "témoignera pour moi", as before a court.

decisions.choice: Mtetezi; ambaye, anayetoka (personal agreement)
decisions.reason: "Mtetezi" (Advocate), as at 14:16 and 26. Roho takes personal agreement ("ambaye", "anayetoka"), as there; the free pronouns "yeye" and "naye" carry the reader setting.

decisions.choice: Đấng Biện Hộ; Thánh Linh của chân lý; "Đấng" and "Ngài" for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The book-wide term for parakletos, as in 14:16 and 14:26; here the setting is plainly testimony. The footnote gives "Đấng Yên Ủi" (Comforter) and "Đấng Trợ Giúp" (Helper). The Spirit is a person, so "Đấng" and "Ngài" under the setting.

decisions.choice: "변호자", "그분" with the honorific, and "증언하다" at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide terms (style guide, section 6): "변호자" for the paraklētos, and "증언하다" for testify, which keeps the courtroom setting of 15:26-27 and 16:8-11. The Spirit is spoken of as a person with the honorific, whatever the gender of the Greek pronouns.

source.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς δὲ μαρτυρεῖτε, ὅτι ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστε.

records.literal_gloss: Also you and testify, because from beginning with me you are.

en.L: And you also testify, because you have been with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from [the] beginning.
en.B: And you also testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because you have been with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the beginning.
en.R: And you also are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses, because you have been with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the very beginning.

es.L: y también {{plural_you:ustedes dan|vosotros dais}} testimonio, porque {{plural_you:han estado|habéis estado}} conmigo desde [el] principio.
es.B: Y también {{plural_you:ustedes dan|vosotros dais}} testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque {{plural_you:han estado|habéis estado}} conmigo desde el principio.
es.R: Y también {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} mis testigos, porque {{plural_you:han estado|habéis estado}} conmigo desde el mismo principio.

fr.L: Et vous aussi, vous rendez témoignage, parce que vous êtes avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} depuis [le] commencement.
fr.B: Et vous aussi, vous rendez témoignage à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet, car vous êtes avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} depuis le commencement.
fr.R: Et vous aussi, vous êtes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} témoins, parce que vous êtes avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} depuis le tout début.

sw.L: Nanyi pia mnashuhudia, kwa sababu mmekuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} tangu mwanzo.
sw.B: Nanyi pia mnashuhudia kuhusu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kwa sababu mmekuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} tangu mwanzo.
sw.R: Nanyi pia ni mashahidi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kwa sababu mmekuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} tangu mwanzo kabisa.

vi.L: Và các con cũng làm chứng, vì các con đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ [lúc] ban đầu.
vi.B: Và các con cũng làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì các con đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ ban đầu.
vi.R: Các con cũng là nhân chứng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì các con đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ngay từ đầu.

ko.L: 그리고 너희도 증언한다. 너희가 처음부터 나와 함께 있어 왔기 때문이다.
ko.B: 너희도 나에 대하여 증언한다. 너희는 처음부터 나와 함께 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 너희도 나의 증인이다. 너희는 처음부터 나와 함께 있었기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: you testify: a statement that the disciples are witnesses, joined with the Spirit
decisions.reason: The form μαρτυρεῖτε can be a statement or a command. Following the promise that the Spirit will testify, a statement fits best: the disciples' witness stands beside the Spirit's (compare Acts 5:32, "we are witnesses, and so is the Holy Spirit"). A command is also possible, and the following "because" could give the reason they are to do it.

decisions.choice: you have been with me from the beginning: a present tense for something that began in the past and goes on
decisions.reason: Greek uses the present "you are" with "from the beginning" for a state that started then and continues now: they were with him from the start and are with him still.

decisions.choice: the beginning: the start of Jesus's public work, when the disciples first followed him
alternatives: the beginning of creation, as in 1:1
decisions.reason: The disciples have been with Jesus since he called them (1:35-51; 16:4). That is what qualifies them as witnesses: they saw and heard for themselves (Acts 1:21-22; 1 John 1:1-3).

decisions.choice: testify about me (B); are my witnesses (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "about me" from 15:26, which the Greek implies. Readable expresses the statement with the noun "witnesses", which says the same thing in plain words (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: acerca de mí (B); mis testigos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: vous êtes avec moi depuis ... (present tense at every level)
alternatives: vous avez été avec moi depuis le commencement
decisions.reason: As in 14:9, French, like the Greek, uses the present with "depuis" for a state that began in the past and still goes on (meaning decision m2), so every level keeps the present where English needs "you have been". Literal brackets the article that French needs and the Greek lacks.

decisions.choice: làm chứng (L, B); nhân chứng (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide key terms for testify and witness.
